title: I'm Not Even an NPC In This Otome Game! Manga Ends
content:
Square Enix 's Manga UP! platform started publishing the final chapter of writer Gyokuro and artist Meno Himeno 's I'm Not Even an NPC In This Otome Game! manga on Tuesday.

Manga UP! describes the story:

Taichi was reincarnated as Isaac, an apprentice gardener in the world of an otome game. But, looking back, Isaac wasn't even part of the game... This is the story of the interweaving lives of the Duke's daughter, Lydia, and a boy who isn't even an NPC.

Himeno launched the manga adaptation of Gyokuro 's light novel on Square Enix 's Manga UP! platform in April 2020. Square Enix shipped the fifth compiled book volume in January 2023.

The series is also available on Comikey and BookWalker .

Gyokuro launched the original novel story on the Shōsetsuka ni Narō platform in December 2018.

title: The Iceblade Sorcerer Shall Rule the World Season 2 Unveils 5 Cast Members
content:
The staff for the second television anime season based on Nana Mikoshiba 's The Iceblade Sorcerer Shall Rule the World ( Hyōken no Majutsushi ga Sekai wo Suberu - Sekai Saikyō no Majutsushi de Aru Shōnen wa, Majutsu Gakuin ga Nyūgaku Suru ) light novel series announced five new cast members on Tuesday. The new cast members is performing in the anime's fifth episode on Thursday.

The newly announced cast members are (image above from left to right, character name romanizations are not confirmed):

• Yūki Wakai as Cathy Alferius

• Toshiyuki Morikawa as Abel Alferius

• Tetsu Inada as Cyril Alferius

• Daiki Hamano as Lard Alferius

• Riona Imaizumi as Mia

The returning cast members include:

• Junya Enoki as Ray White

• Iori Saeki as Amelia Ros

• Akira Sekine as Ariane Olgren

• Azumi Waki as Rebecca Bradley

• Kaede Hondo as Clarisse Cleveland

• Yūichirō Umehara as Evi Armstrong

• Kōhei Amasaki as Albert Allium

• Atsumi Tanezaki as Stella White

• Sōichirō Hoshi as Lucas Forst

• Haruka Shiraishi as Lizelotte Eden

Previously announced new cast members are:

• Hana Hishikawa as Olivia Arnold

• Ryōhei Kimura as Julius Orphe

• Aoi Koga as Bianca Miller

• Konomi Kohara as Emma Clarke

• Shiki Aoki as Maria Bradley

• Kazuyuki Okitsu as Marius Basset

Miyu Kubota voices Elisa Griffith. Kubota is replacing Nana Harumura , who retired from voice acting in January due to health reasons.

Masahiro Takata is returning to direct the second season, and is also returning to write and oversee the series scripts, and serve as sound director. Zero-G is now animating the series ( Cloud Hearts animated the first season). Other scriptwriters include Tomoko Shinozuka (returning from the first season) and Takahito Ōnishi ( Whisper Me a Love Song , My Happy Marriage ). Mariko Kawamoto ( Magica Wars ) is the new character designer, replacing Makoto Shimojima .

Sizuk performs the opening theme song "Diamond Dust," and Maaya Uchida performs the ending theme song "Compression :[."

The second season premiered on TBS on October 8 at 1:23 a.m. and also started airing on BS11 on October 9 at 11:00 p.m. Crunchyroll streams the anime as it airs.

Kodansha USA Publishing licensed the manga, and it describes the story:

The Arnold Academy of Magic is a school for the elite...and Ray White is just your ordinary guy. In fact, he doesn't seem particularly skilled with magic at all, and is a bit of a klutz. Which is why he has nothing to do with the rumor that one of the great magicians, the Iceblade Sorcerer, is a member of the incoming class...right?

The first season of the television anime premiered in January 2023. Crunchyroll streamed the anime as it aired in Japan, and also streamed an English dub .

Mikoshiba's original story launched on the Shōsetsuka ni Narō (Let's Become Novelists) website in October 2019. The light novel series debuted in July 2020, with illustrations by Riko Korie . Kodansha publishes the light novels in print in Japan.

Norihito Sasaki 's manga adaptation launched on Magazine Pocket in June 2020, and ended in January 2024. The manga's 16th and final volume shipped in April 2024.

A Hyōken no Majutsushi ga Sekai wo Suberu II : Sekai Saikyō no Majutsushi de Aru Shōnen wa, Majutsu Gakuin ga Nyūgaku Suru sequel manga launched on May 27. Nao Kagami illustrates the manga and Ishiya Ōgane is in charge of composition. Niconico Manga publishes the manga under Kodansha 's " Suiyōbi no Sirius " label.

title: 'Hyouken no Majutsushi ga Sekai wo Suberu II' Announces Additional Cast
content:
The official website for the television anime adaptation of Nana Mikoshiba 's Hyouken no Majutsushi ga Sekai wo Suberu ( The Iceblade Sorcerer Shall Rule the World ) light novel announced five additional cast members for the second season on Tuesday. The new season premiered on TBS on October 9 at 1.28 a.m., followed by BS11 at 11.00 p.m. on the same day.

Cast Cathy Alphelius: Yuuki Wakai ( Kakegurui ) Abel Alphelius: Toshiyuki Morikawa ( Nohara Hiroshi: Hiru Meshi no Ryuugi ) Cyril Alphelius: Tetsu Inada ( Tsubasa Chronicle ) Rald Alphelius: Daiki Hamano ( Darling in the FranXX ) Mia: Riona Imaizumi

Masahiro Takata ( Nageki no Bourei wa Intai shitai ) returns to direct the second season, while also taking over series composition and sound director at Zero-G . Masahiro Takata ( Bananya ), Tomoko Shinozuka ( Wotaku ni Koi wa Muzukashii ), Takahito Oonishi (Watashi no Shiawase na Kekkon) are penning the script. Mariko Kawamoto ( Mahou Shoujo Taisen ) is designing the characters, replacing Makoto Shimojima . Tatsuhiko Saiki ( Otome Game no Hametsu Flag shika Nai Akuyaku Reijou ni Tensei shiteshimatta... X ) and Natsumi Tabuchi ( Adachi to Shimamura ) are composing the music.

Produced by Cloud Hearts , the first season aired as a 12-episode series in Winter 2023. Crunchyroll simulcast the anime with subtitles and dubs in multiple languages.

Mikoshiba began writing the light novel on the Shousetsuka ni Narou website in October 2019. Kodansha began publishing the novel under its Ranobe Bunko imprint in July 2020, with illustrations by Riko Korie . The ninth volume was published on June 2, with the tenth volume scheduled for a December 2 release.

Norihito Sasaki began a manga adaptation in Magazine pocket in June 2020. Kodansha released the 16th volume in April 2024.

A sequel manga adaptation by Nao Kagami, titled Hyouken no Majutsushi ga Sekai wo Suberu II began serialization on the Suiyoubi no Sirius web service on May 27.

Kodansha USA licensed the manga in English in October 2021. The 13th volume went on sale on June 2.

title: Live-Action Quiztopia Series Unveils Trailer, Key Art
content:
Netflix Japan revealed the main trailer and key art for Quiztopia , its eight-episode live-action series of Reiichi Sugimoto and Shinkichi Kato 's Kokumin Quiz ( National Quiz ) manga, on Tuesday. The English-subtitled trailer includes scenes that feature 8,000 extras, as well as the in-story commercials with the government's propaganda messages.

Netflix describes the story:

The story takes place in an alternate Japan where Quiztopia, a National Quiz show, has become the country's supreme governing authority. Under the National Quiz Law, any contestant who survives the quiz can have virtually any wish granted by the government — wealth, fame, the death of an enemy, the erasure of a criminal record, even ownership of a national landmark. The broadcast draws enormous audiences, and even the brutal forced labor awaiting eliminated contestants is treated as entertainment in this cheerfully dystopian society. At the center of it all is KK ( Takayuki Yamada ), the show's iconic host and the public's chief provocateur — who comes into contact with a group plotting to bring down Quiztopia, setting off an incident that could awaken people consumed by this seductive nightmare.

Takayuki Yamada (live-action Densha Otoko 's "Train Man," Bakuman. 's Akira Hattori, Gintama's Elizabeth) stars in the series as KK.

The cast includes:

• Masahiro Takashima as as Commander Murakoshi, who leads the Reward and Punishment Squad responsible for carrying out penalties determined by the quiz results

• Eiko Koike as Shoko Kamijo, the producer behind Quiztopia

• Riko Ishida as Marii, a mysterious girl intent on killing KK

• Kana Kurashina as Ayako, Mari's mother and a central figure in the story;

• Kōji Seto as Seiji Nanbara, an activist plotting Quiztopia's downfall

• Renji Ishibashi as Takeshi Gokumazawa, the Prime Minister of Japan

• Rin Kataoka

• Yuzu Aoki

• Naruki Matsukawa

• Yūki Imai

• Shunsuke Daitō

• Akira Maehara

• Hoshi no Disco

• First Summer Uika

• Keiko Horiuchi

• Toshinori Omi

Teruyuki Yoshida (live-action An Older Guy's VR First Love , My Brother’s Husband ) is directing the series, and is also co-writing the scripts with Maggy. Yasunori Nishiki is composing the music.

The series p remieres on Netflix on December 17.

Sugimoto and Kato serialized the manga in Kodansha 's Morning magazine from 1993 to 1995. Kodansha published four compiled book volumes for the manga. Ohta Publishing re-released the manga in two compiled book volumes in 2001.

title: Demon Slayer Failed Where Jujutsu Kaisen and My Hero Academia Won & It’s Not Even Close
content:
Warning: This article contains spoilers from the Demon Slayer manga! There’s no denying that Demon Slayer is one of the most popular anime and manga franchises of all time despite being a fairly new series. The franchise has set such a high standard for the industry that it will be difficult for upcoming series to overcome in the next few years. Regardless of its popularity and breathtaking anime visuals, the story has its fair share of issues. The thing that makes this series truly special is the emotional depth and the lovable characters who fans can’t help but adore. However, despite that, the manga is still controversial for one of its most rushed final arcs and the finale.

It’s been more than six years since the manga reached its conclusion, but the ending couldn’t be saved at all. The manga killed off half of the main cast in the showdown between the Demon Slayers and the demons, wiping out almost the entire Demon Slayer Corps, leaving many disappointed as the victory didn’t even feel worth celebrating. Furthermore, Demon Slayer didn’t focus enough on the direct aftermath of the final battle , but instead skipped into the modern era. This is something where Jujutsu Kaisen and My Hero Academia excelled at since both stories were expanded after the finale, something which Demon Slayer could have benefitted from.

Demon Slayer Needs to Expand Its Story After Finale

The initial phase of the story moved at a steady pace, but things changed for the worse in the Infinity Castle Arc. The continuous and intense battles were thrilling enough initially until fans realized that the series planned to kill off most of the main characters by the end. Not to mention that the epilogue was barely one chapter long with a time skip, featuring the reincarnations or descendants of the beloved characters. The manga didn’t delve deeper into the time skip either, which made it all the more confusing about what the story was trying to portray . Instead of focusing on the surviving characters after the final battle, the story ended too soon, while making sure it would never return with a sequel or even a prequel or a spin-off, which seems like a wasted opportunity.

The fate of Giyu and Sanemi was also left for fans’ discussion since the Demon Slayer Mark itself was never properly explained. There were several theories regarding the Mark, but it’s most likely that both characters never managed to live past 25, something which the manga never covered. The closed narrative would have been perfect if only the main battle hadn’t ended in such a rush. The time skip featured a world where demons no longer exist, which is why there’s no point in continuing the story further. While the ending can barely be fixed at this point since the creator doesn’t plan on returning to Shonen Jump , the anime can still make up for it with original scenes.

Jujutsu Kaisen and My Hero Academia Nailed the Endings With the Story’s Continuation

Out of these three series, My Hero Academia has by far the most satisfying conclusion since the main story itself was pretty well-written without being rushed at all. Even after that, Kohei Horikoshi returned with extra chapters and explored the story through the main characters. The story didn’t focus on decades of time-skip, leaving us with no option to know how the beloved characters lived after the final battle. While My Hero Academia doesn’t have an official sequel, these extra chapters and one-shots, which were also adapted into an anime, gave the perfect farewell to the story.

On the other hand, Jujutsu Kaisen ended its main story on a rather controversial note with several unanswered questions. The ending can’t be considered good, and even the anime adaptation can’t save it at this point. However, the sequel manga, Jujutsu Kaisen Modulo , gave the story another life by exploring the world-building and solving the biggest issue in the world of curses. While the sequel story primarily focused on new characters, it also resolved the fate of the beloved characters, which is the biggest reason why the sequel made the ending a little bit better. Demon Slayer ended after the demons’ defeat, which is why there was no more room for conflict.

However, conflict isn’t the only way to continue the story since the characters and their dreams could always be explored in a much more peaceful world. Not to mention that there’s always an option for a prequel as well since the Sengoku Era is still pretty much shrouded in mystery. A story centering around Yoriichi would definitely become a hit since he is already one of the most beloved characters. Regardless, the ending isn’t bad at all, although it could’ve ended before the time skip so there could be room to fix the rushed conclusion that wasn’t more important than the unanswered questions.

Do you wish Demon Slayer had received a sequel or an additional chapter, and what would you have liked to see explored after the ending? Share your thoughts in the comments below!

title: Urban Myth Dissolution Center Manga Ends
content:
Emi Ishikawa announced on X (formerly Twitter ) that Toshi Densetsu Kaitai Center: Parallel File ( Urban Myth Dissolution Center : parallelfile, the manga adaptation of Shueisha Game's Urban Myth Dissolution Center game, has ended in the December issue of Shueisha 's Ribon magazine on Monday.

Ishikawa launched the manga adaptation in Shueisha 's Ribon magazine in April 2025. Shueisha shipped the third compiled book volume on August 19.

The Urban Myth Dissolution Center game launched for PC via Steam in February 2025. The game's Steam page describes the story:

The Urban Myth Dissolution Center – your one-stop solution for dissolving and dealing with cursed relics, monstrous oddities, and dimensional anomalies! Take on cases revolving around urban myths as Azami Fukurai, the heroine, under the supervision of Ayumu Meguriya, Level S psychic and Center Director...

The game launched for iOS and Android mobile devices in March. The game's Nintendo Switch 2 edition launched on October 28. The Switch 2 edition of Urban Myth Dissolution Center adds features for the Joy-Con 2's mouse controls and a gallery to revisit the game's artwork at any time.

title: 3 Major Isekai You Can Only Watch on HIDIVE
content:
HIDIVE has earned its reputation as an anime streaming platform, and these three exclusive isekai titles prove it. Choosing an anime streaming platform and a genre can be overwhelming, especially in this modern era, where new streaming platforms and genres seem to emerge almost every now and then. However, some combinations can always work.

Isekai has long been one of the oldest and most popular genres in the anime world, with countless titles available to watch. With such an abundance of choices, finding the right anime can be difficult. However, pairing the genre with a streaming platform like HIDIVE gives fans a more selective range of isekai titles to explore, and these three exclusives are proof of that.

title: Drama Queen Manga Ends in 4 Chapters
content:
Kuraku Ichikawa announced on X (formerly Twitter ) on Monday that their Drama Queen manga will end in four chapters.

MANGA Plus publishes the series in English and describes the story:

Hate brings pain to the world. After saving the earth, aliens have taken up residence with the humans in Japan. Nomamoto, a factory worker with an abusive alien boss, one day meets Kitami, who tells her his own family was killed by aliens. The two quickly forge a friendship, but one day Kitami does the unthinkable...

Ichikawa launched the series on Shueisha 's Shonen Jump+ in December 2024. Shueisha shipped the seventh compiled book volume on September 4.

title: Trigun Anime Gets New Novel This Winter
content:
The autumn issue of Shueisha 's Jump SQ. RISE magazine announced on Thursday that the Trigun franchise will get a new novel written in collaboration between series creator Yasuhiro Nightow and Trigun Stampede writer Takehiko Oxi titled Trigun Manuscript this winter. The series will be based on the world of the Trigun Stampede and Trigun Stargaze anime.

The Trigun Stargaze anime premiered on TV Tokyo and its affiliated channels on January 10. Crunchyroll streamed the anime as it aired, along with an English dub .

Trigun Stargaze is the previously announced " final phase " of the Trigun Stampede anime , set 2.5 years after the end of Trigun Stampede .

Trigun Stampede premiered in Japan in January 2023. Crunchyroll streamed the series as it aired and is also streaming an English dub .

Madhouse 's previous television anime adaptation aired for 26 episodes in Japan in 1998. The anime launched in North America for home video in 2000. Geneon Entertainment (formerly Pioneer ) originally released the series on DVD, but Funimation has since licensed the series and released it on Blu-ray Disc and DVD. The series is now streaming on Crunchyroll following Sony 's Funimation Global Group 's acquisition of Crunchyroll from AT&T. Cartoon Network 's Adult Swim programming block aired the anime in 2003.

The Trigun anime adapts Yasuhiro Nightow 's manga of the same name. The manga ran in Tokuma Shoten 's Monthly Shonen Captain magazine from 1995 to 1997. The manga returned with Trigun Maximum in Shōnengahōsha 's Young King Ours magazine later in 1997 and ran until 2007. Dark Horse Comics has released the manga in English.

The Trigun: Badlands Rumble anime film debuted in April 2010 and was the first new Trigun animation in over a decade.

title: Crunchyroll Releases New English Dub for Two Legendary Shonen Jump Movies After 21 Years
content:
The two classic Shonen Jump movies got their anticipated English dub release by Crunchyroll. Over the decades, Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump magazine has serialized several legendary manga series, most of which ended up getting their anime adaptations. The same goes for the timeless classic, The Prince of Tennis , written and illustrated by Takeshi Konomi. While the anime made its return in September this year as part of the Fall 2026 anime lineup , Crunchyroll released the English dub of The Prince of Tennis: A Gift from Atobe and The Prince of Tennis: Two Samurais, The First Game . Both movies were originally released on January 29th, 2005, but fans only had access to the Japanese audio with English subtitles until now.

These short movies added their English dub on October 14th, 2026. While Crunchyroll didn’t officially announce the release, @AnimeDubUpdates on X spotted it and shared it with fans. While A Gift from Otobe is only 30 minutes long, the other movie has double the runtime, and they were both co-aired in the theatres in Japan before getting their worldwide streaming release. Neither of these movies is considered canon since they don’t officially adapt the source material, but considering their critical acclaim, they’re both a must-watch for every fan.

The Prince of Tennis II Made Its Comeback This Year With a New Season

The Prince of Tennis II U-17 World Cup: Final Member Selection Match is the latest season of the anime , and the first installment since the manga’s conclusion. The Final Member Selection Match premiered on Crunchyroll on September 30th, 2026, and it has released five episodes so far. The anime is streaming across the regions of North America, Central America, South America, Europe, Africa, Oceania, the Middle East, CIS, and the Indian subcontinent. Along with the subbed release date, the platform also released the English dub, which is two weeks behind the original schedule. The latest season is scheduled for 13 episodes, after which we can expect to know more about what the studio has planned for the anime’s future. Fans can also catch up to the previous seasons that are streaming on the platform. The anime is returning after two years with better visuals and production as the story heads closer to its ending.

The Prince of Tennis II Anime Isn’t Ending Anytime Soon

The manga originally began serialization in 2009 and ended in 2008, but it took only one year for Konomi to return with a sequel in Shueisha’s Jump Square magazine. The Prince of Tennis II reached its conclusion in 2024 , marking the end of this long-running franchise. While the main story in the manga is already over, the anime still has a huge chunk of story left to adapt. The Semifinal primarily focuses on the match against the German national team as they try to reach the finals for the first time in Japan’s tennis history. Additionally, the latest season directly picks up from where the story left off as the Team Japan players face off against their old rivals to earn spots in the lineup for the World Cup final.
